n: Woe to you, destroyer, who have never been destroyed; betrayer, who have never been betrayed! When you finish destroying, you’ll be destroyed. This is aimed at Assyria, which broke its agreement with Hezekiah.

f.g: You destroyer — likely Assyria under Sennacherib.

n: The people pray: Lord, be gracious to us; we have waited for You. Be our strength every morning and our salvation in trouble.

f.w: be thou their arm every morning

n: At the thunder of God’s voice, peoples flee; when He rises up, nations scatter.
The enemy’s plunder will be stripped as if by swarming caterpillars and leaping locusts.
The Lord is exalted, dwelling on high; He fills Zion with justice and righteousness.

f.w: he hath filled Zion with judgment and righteousness

n: He will be the stability of your times, a rich store of salvation, wisdom, and knowledge. Reverence for the Lord is Zion’s treasure.

f.w: the fear of the LORD is his treasure

n: Isaiah describes the crisis: Judah’s brave men cry in the streets, and the envoys who sought peace weep bitterly — their negotiations with Assyria failed.
The highways are empty and travelers have stopped. The enemy has broken the treaty, despised the cities, and respects no one.
The land mourns and withers. Lebanon is ashamed, Sharon is a desert, and Bashan and Carmel lose their leaves — even the most fertile regions suffer.
“Now I will rise,” says the Lord. “Now I will be exalted; now I will lift Myself up.” God steps in at the darkest moment.
The enemy’s plans are like being pregnant with chaff and giving birth to straw; their own fiery breath will consume them.
The peoples will be burned like lime in a kiln, like cut thornbushes set ablaze.

f.g: Limestone was burned to make lime — reduced to white ash.

n: You who are far away, hear what God has done; you who are near, recognize His might.
The sinners in Zion are terrified, and trembling grips the godless: “Who among us can live with the consuming fire? Who can dwell with everlasting burnings?” God’s glorious presence is like fire.

The answer: the one who lives righteously and speaks honestly, rejects profit from oppression, refuses bribes, won’t listen to plots of violence, and shuts his eyes to evil. Compare the temple-entrance questions in the Psalms.

f.w: shaketh his hands from holding of bribes
shutteth his eyes from seeing evil

n: That person will dwell on the heights; his refuge will be a mountain fortress, and he will always have bread and water.
Your eyes will see the King in His beauty and behold a land stretching far away. The righteous will one day see the Lord.

f.w: Thine eyes shall see the king in his beauty
the land that is very far off
f.g: A wide, expansive land — no longer hemmed in by enemies.

n: You will remember past terror and ask, “Where is the official who counted, who weighed the tribute, who counted the towers?” The Assyrian officials will be gone.

f.g: The one who weighed tribute money.

n: You will no longer see the fierce invaders with their strange, unintelligible language.
Look at Zion, city of our festivals! Jerusalem will be a peaceful home, a tent never moved, whose stakes and cords will never break. Latter-day Saints draw the term “stake” from this image.

f.w: a tabernacle that shall not be taken down

f.g: Tent pegs that hold a tent firmly in place.

n: There the glorious Lord will be for us a place of broad rivers and streams, but no enemy warships will sail on them. God is both supply and protection.
The Lord is our Judge, our Lawgiver, and our King; He will save us. He fills every role of government perfectly.
The enemy is like a ship with loose rigging that cannot hold its mast or spread its sail. Its treasure will be divided so abundantly that even the lame will carry off plunder.
No one in Zion will say, “I am sick,” and the people there will be forgiven their sins. Physical and spiritual healing go together.
